key_insight: A physics-informed, latent-regularized U-Net can segment pathological lower-limb muscle MRI accurately even when manual labels are sparse.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help generate patient-specific musculoskeletal segmentations for modeling and analysis without requiring large expert-annotated datasets.
method: Transfer learning from healthy MRI to initialize the model
Add latent-space anatomical regularization to preserve plausible shapes
Use physics-informed losses enforcing equilibrium, near-incompressibility, and smooth deformation fields
evidence_signal: Evaluated on MRI from 50 participants with cerebral palsy across 15 lower-limb structures, with 3D Dice scores ranging from 0.750 to 0.943 and generally low surface-distance errors.
watch_item: Performance and plausibility were shown in a specific cerebral palsy MRI setting, so broader generalization and implementation on other anatomies or scanners still need validation.
paper_title: 3D Segmentation of Pathological Muscle with a Physics-Informed Latent-Regularized U-Net
